## Result

- Skill: code-review.
- Status: completed.
- Artifacts changed: docs/changes/2026-09-09-release-model-source-consolidation/reviews/code-review-m2-r1.json.
- Open blockers: four required M2 implementation corrections below; no upstream owner decision needed.
- Next stage: return to route for M2 review-resolution and bounded implementation correction, then independent reassessment.
- Review status: changes-requested.
- Material findings: release-m2-f1, release-m2-f2, release-m2-f3, release-m2-f4.
- Recording status: recorded upon successful primary persistence.
- Recording blocker: none.
- Review record: docs/changes/2026-09-09-release-model-source-consolidation/reviews/code-review-m2-r1.json.
- Assessment scope: milestone.
- Reviewed milestone: M2, 3dcea08b through frozen working-tree M2 slice over M1 3dcea08b (no final M2 commit yet).
- Milestone closeout: resolution-needed.
- Remaining implementation milestones: M3 and M4 after M2 correction/review.
- Required review-resolution: yes.
- Finding IDs: release-m2-f1 through release-m2-f4.
- Verify readiness: not-claimed; incomplete milestones and required corrections remain.

## Independence, authority and inspected scope

The independent reviewer /root/independent_delivery_review authored none of M2 implementation or tests. Earlier participation was independent Delivery/M1 assessment, not engineering authorship. No engineering, activity or work record was edited in this review. Exact subjects above include the complete M2 implementation slice, producer/consumer helpers, four governing Design members, primary plan and execution evidence. Approved/current design-review-r4 and delivery-review-r1 retain their exact normative subjects; M1 code-review-m1-r3 is the upstream milestone assessment. Earlier contextual implementation snapshots keep their old meaning, not a claim that changed source hashes were reviewed previously.

M2 adds protected approval checks, immutable candidate execution, GitHub/npm boundary adapters, version-scoped Git CAS evidence, generated standing/companion metadata and tests discovered by the retained entrypoint. The published-status validator addition is additive; prior pending validation remains the default. The live workflow remains unchanged, as allocated to M3. No real publication, credential/configuration change, installation into a customer project or source retirement occurred. Review covers M2 and its M1 interactions only; final whole-change review remains mandatory.

## Proof and limits

Author handoff: current frozen focused proof `python -m unittest release_execution_tests` (scripts import path) passed 19 tests in 34.001s, /tmp/release-m2-focused.log. Earlier `python scripts/test-release-transaction.py` passed 140 tests in 88.086s before final companion completeness changes. A later full run /tmp/release-m2-complete.log failed 7 errors from the incorrect nested-metadata parser and is preserved as failed evidence. The author corrected that parser using the existing metadata parser and ran the current focused proof. The exact frozen full suite is still running at /tmp/release-m2-handoff.log when this required-changes assessment is recorded; no final suite success or milestone approval is inferred. The author will record final observed proof separately. The implementation is already known to need the independently demonstrated corrections, so unfinished broad validation does not suppress those findings or require an inconclusive overall judgment. The author also identified uncaught subprocess TimeoutExpired; it must be covered by the uncertainty correction and rereview, not silently treated as a current pass.


Reviewer direct counterexamples used python heredoc imports from scripts/release_execution_tests.py and actual release_execution validators/executor/GitEvidence: identical provider artifact accepted two candidate IDs; successful first tag followed by unavailable observation was reported before-publication; retained timing validator rejected generated phases: []; and reporting-failure recovery removed the earlier failure from local/durable events while maintaining write counts. Temporary isolated sources/remotes were cleaned, external services substituted, no source fixes made. These are targeted independent observations, not a full new public release or CI run. Existing tests support CAS exclusion, no duplicate writes on confirmed boundaries, partial asset recovery, tamper/rejected-approval denial, retained tarball/OIDC arguments and actual public-evidence/metadata validators; passing coverage does not close the demonstrated gaps.

The provider endpoints were cross-checked against GitHub's primary workflow-run API reference, https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/workflow-runs#get-the-review-history-for-a-workflow-run. That read-only documentation check grants no configured remote protection or runtime publication proof.

## Checklist

| Item | Result | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Spec alignment | concern | REL-SR-10/14/15/18/19/23/24 and TG-03/04 gaps in f1-f4. |
| Test coverage | concern | Meaningful executor/CAS/validator cases pass, but four direct counterexamples are absent from assertions. |
| Edge cases | concern | First-write unknown outcome and recovery-history preservation fail despite ordinary retry protection. |
| Error handling | concern | Bounded suppression and observation-first retries exist; uncertainty/report recovery are misrepresented. |
| Architecture boundaries | concern | Real external substitutes and existing owners reused; provider artifact metadata is not connected to candidate bytes. |
| Compatibility | pass | Existing helper entrypoints and pending-publication validator default retained; no historical sources/records removed. |
| Security/privacy | concern | OIDC retained tarball/no token fallback and bounded diagnostics supported; exact artifact authority remains incomplete. |
| Derived artifact currency | concern | M1 sealing, archive/public tree checks and generated evidence validators remain; approval provenance and emitted diagnostic currency need correction. |
| Unrelated changes | pass | M2 slice only; no hosted activation, source retirement or unrelated refactor. |
| Validation evidence | concern | Named suite evidence is bounded and truthful, but it does not establish the four missing protections. |

## Handoff

Return to route for correction ownership; this reviewer does not mutate progression. M2 is not closed. Required findings are recorded before engineering corrections and require independent reassessment. No new Design/Delivery decision is necessary for the bounded fixes; if implementation proposes a new authority or representation policy, return to its owner. No final whole-change, Verify, hosted success or PR readiness is claimed.

## Finding release-m2-f1

- Finding ID: release-m2-f1
- Severity: major
- Location: scripts/release_execution.py:validate_approval / execute_candidate; scripts/release_provider.py:GitHubApprovals.fetch
- Evidence: Provider metadata and the caller-supplied candidate ID are validated independently: nothing downloads or hashes the referenced provider artifact or proves that the local sealed set was extracted from it. Direct invocation of the actual validator accepts both candidate a*64 and replacement d*64 under the identical artifact ID/digest, source/run and approval responses, after changing the caller candidate/binding ID together. The fixture digest c*64 has no byte relationship to its local candidate. The author confirms that no other extraction/binding component exists. REL-SR-23/24 and M2 TG-03 require this authority boundary in the executor; physical hosted wiring may remain M3.
- Required outcome: Bind the local exact candidate set to independently fetched immutable provider-artifact bytes/digest before any evidence/public write. Verify extraction safety and manifest/local-content identity; fail closed for substituted candidate contents, changed binding IDs, expired/changed provider artifacts and unsafe archives. Have M3 consume this tested M2 boundary. Do not treat a metadata comparison or caller-supplied digest as byte provenance.
- Safe resolution path: bounded implementation correction and direct regression proof, then independent reassessment.
- needs-decision rationale: none; approved contract already requires the outcome.

## Finding release-m2-f2

- Finding ID: release-m2-f2
- Severity: major
- Location: scripts/release_execution.py:execute_candidate failure classification and render_standing
- Evidence: The failure handler classifies solely by whether confirmed observations exist. A direct actual-executor/local-Git counterexample publishes the fixture tag, then makes all tag observations unavailable. The public tag exists and writes=[tag], but stored status is failed-before-publication and standing status failed-before-publish; events show write-intent and unknown. This falsely claims no publication before failure precisely when the first irreversible result is unknown. REL-SR-10/14/15 and TG-04 require failed-during/uncertain meaning.
- Required outcome: Retain a truthful uncertain/during-publication outcome whenever a write may have happened and cannot be authoritatively resolved, including the first tag boundary and lost-response/timeout paths. Preserve intent and uncertainty without inventing a completed public identity. Prove reporting and subsequent observation-first recovery without duplicate writes.
- Safe resolution path: bounded implementation correction and direct regression proof, then independent reassessment.
- needs-decision rationale: none; approved contract already requires the outcome.

## Finding release-m2-f3

- Finding ID: release-m2-f3
- Severity: minor
- Location: scripts/release_execution.py:timing_projection / persist
- Evidence: timing_projection always emits phases: [] as release-timing-v1 and execute_candidate does not run/report the diagnostic validator. Direct invocation of the existing validate_release_timing_evidence on a generated document reports all six required phases missing. A completed execution therefore silently emits diagnostically invalid telemetry. REL-SR-18 permits nonblocking absent timing but explicitly requires malformed emitted timing be reported separately; REL-SR-19 retains the format.
- Required outcome: Preserve actual available observations and assess/report emitted timing defects separately from publication correctness. Reuse the retained timing diagnostic owner, or emit a valid supported incomplete representation where the owner permits it. Do not invent missing durations, redefine the format silently, or turn diagnostic absence into a publication gate. Add direct proof for emitted malformed/absent telemetry and required facts continuing independently.
- Safe resolution path: bounded implementation correction and direct regression proof, then independent reassessment.
- needs-decision rationale: none; approved contract already requires the outcome.

## Finding release-m2-f4

- Finding ID: release-m2-f4
- Severity: major
- Location: scripts/release_execution.py:execute_candidate previous-state selection and persist observed-outcome.json
- Evidence: After durable reporting fails, the local observation bundle is the only copy of the reporting failure. Recovery ignores that bundle and initializes from older Git evidence, then overwrites observed-outcome.json on its first persist. Using the existing FailingStore(save >=7) through the actual executor, attempt 1 retains a reporting/incomplete event; attempt 2 completes with failure=none and no reporting event in durable or local history. Public writes correctly remain one per boundary, but the failure/recovery evidence is erased. REL-SR-15/24 and M2 TG-04 explicitly require preservation/reconciliation of failed attempts.
- Required outcome: Validate and preserve/reconcile retained observations before recovery overwrites them, retaining their exact candidate/attempt identity and failure meaning in durable history or an existing bounded companion. Do not let untrusted local observations authorize publication. Prove failed-reporting recovery preserves the earlier failure and actual outcomes, keeps unrelated records intact, and performs no second public write.
- Safe resolution path: bounded implementation correction and direct regression proof, then independent reassessment.
- needs-decision rationale: none; approved contract already requires the outcome.
